properties.name: MEASURED across 93 sessions of two OTHER reflow2 projects: 88% of skill loads had no slash command behind them, so agents DO self-invoke at scale — and what predicts a skill's load count is being named in the always-injected SessionStart hook, not being in the served catalogue
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 over the Claude Code transcripts on the peer box (ajs77), read-only: `dev-storyflow` 91 sessions / 4157 real user turns / 21993 tool calls / 5240 reflow2 tool calls, spanning 2026-07-29 to 2026-08-29; `OpenLotR2` 2 sessions / 52 user turns / 440 reflow2 tool calls. 175 and 7 skill loads respectively, via `get_skill` (151) and the `Skill` tool (24).

═══ ⭐ IT REFUTES THE STRONG FORM OF fact:a-skill-is-loaded-only-when-something-already-in-hand-demands-it ═══

That node says an agent loads a skill when something already in its hand demands it "and otherwise substantially not at all", generalising from ONE session where 3 of 5 loads were user-typed. At n=93 sessions the shape is the opposite: **154 of 175 loads (88%) had NO matching slash command anywhere earlier in the session.** Agents self-invoke reflow2 skills constantly. Where a matching command did exist, the median gap was 1 user turn, so those are genuinely command-driven and the split is clean.

The WEAK form survives and is what the data supports: loading is driven by an instruction already in context. reflow2 HAS such a mechanism — the SessionStart hook and the MCP server instructions — and it is working. The earlier node's error was treating 'no reflow2 TOOL demands a skill' as 'nothing demands a skill'.

═══ ⭐⭐ WHAT ACTUALLY PREDICTS THE COUNT: THE HOOK, NOT THE CATALOGUE ═══

    skill              loads   /cmd typed   ratio
    where-am-i            42        5        8.4x   ← NAMED IN THE SessionStart HOOK
    brainstorm            22       10        2.2x
    capture-session       19       18        1.1x   ← essentially all user-typed
    link-artifacts        15        0         —
    capture-intent        15        0         —
    revise-design         12        0         —

The MCP server instructions name ALL 23 skills and usage across them is 42..0 — a catalogue that lists everything predicts nothing. The SessionStart hook names only three (genesis, adopt, where-am-i), and `where-am-i` is the most-loaded skill by a factor of two over anything else, self-invoked 8.4x more often than it is asked for. The other two hook-named skills are one-time by nature (genesis 0, adopt 2), which is the expected reading rather than a counterexample.

⭐ This is direct evidence for `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue`: an always-injected surface moves behaviour, a catalogue read once does not.

═══ NEVER LOADED IN 91 SESSIONS ═══

ci-gate, genesis, kpp-proposal, link-ideas, optimize, parallel-work, plan-increments, root-cause.

🛑 FOUR OF THOSE EIGHT ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING. `genesis` and `ci-gate` are one-time setup and the project is long past both; `adopt` at 2 fits the same shape. `root-cause` shipped in v0.42.0 on 2026-08-28 and could not have been used in a window that mostly precedes it. The four that are genuinely unexplained by situation are **kpp-proposal, link-ideas, optimize, parallel-work, plan-increments** (five, on a stricter reading).

═══ ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ═══

- Whether a never-loaded skill went unused because nothing triggered it or because its SITUATION never arose. Nothing here separates those, and for plan-increments and parallel-work the situation genuinely may not have arisen. This is the same unused-vs-unreachable ambiguity `dec:bl-155` names for tools.
- Causation for the hook. `where-am-i` is also the most generically useful skill in the set, so hook-presence and intrinsic usefulness are confounded. A second skill added to the hook would test it, and that is the cheap discriminating experiment.
- Attribution was measured as loads-per-skill against commands-for-that-same-skill, NOT by turn adjacency. Two earlier adjacency-based passes returned a false 100% self-invoked because Claude Code records tool results as `type: user` and records a slash command and its expansion as two separate user turns, either of which resets a naive 'previous user turn' flag. The ratio method avoids both.
- OpenLotR2 at 2 sessions is far too small to read alone; it is reported for shape only.
